# API reference

The public types of the three libraries you can reference from your own program. For the task-shaped walk-through, with code that compiles, see [Embed nfty in your program](../../how-to/embed-nfty.md); for the roll alone, [Ticket and Menu API](../ticket-api.md).

| Assembly | Types | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| [`Nfty.Ticket`](nfty-ticket/index.md) | 49 | The roll, and nothing else. `net10.0`, no NuGet packages, no imaging library: reference this alone to decide what an asset is - recipe, variants, rolled color, DNA - on a server or in an engine. |
| [`Nfty.Core`](nfty-core/index.md) | 183 | The whole engine: archives, validation, generation, rendering, Sets, export, sealing, statistics. Depends on Nfty.Ticket and ImageSharp. |
| [`Nfty.Model`](nfty-model/index.md) | 31 | Rise: pixel art to 3D. Voxel meshes, glTF writing and reading. Depends on Nfty.Core. |

## Namespaces are not assemblies

`Nfty.Ticket.dll` declares types in the namespaces `Nfty.Ticket`, `Nfty.Core.Generation`, `Nfty.Core.Imaging` and `Nfty.Core.Model`. That is deliberate: those types began life in `Nfty.Core` and keeping their names meant no consumer's `using` changed when the roll moved into its own dependency-free assembly. Each page names the assembly a type ships in, so you know which DLL to reference.

## How these pages are made

From the `///` comments in the source and the public surface of the built assemblies, by `python tools/api-docs/build.py`. They are not edited by hand; change the comment and regenerate. Members that are internal or private do not appear. A method page shows the declaration, then the documentation the author wrote.
